descricao: Eurostars Funding for international SME-led research and development Eurostars is part of the European Partnership on Innovative SMEs. The partnership is co-funded by the European Union through Horizon Europe . Eurostars is an international funding programme for collaborative research and development (R&D) projects led by innovative small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). As the world’s largest SME R&D funding programme, Eurostars supports the creation of innovative products, processes, and services for commercialisation. You can use Eurostars to access public funding for international R&D projects. The programme has some unique features: Work with international partners to strengthen your R&D Develop new business relationships Be guided from idea to commercialisation with advice and support from a network of national project coordinators Eurostars provides funding to international R&D projects. Projects must be led by an SME or startup from a Eurostars country or region, and the project consortium must also include at least one other independent organisation from another Eurostars country. Partners in the consortium can include any type of organisation. Eurostars funding comes from National Funding Bodies, which are ministries or funding agencies in each Eurostars country or region, and from the European Commission. National Funding Bodies determine how much funding is available, the funding rate per type of company, and which activities are eligible based on national rules. Your project must meet seven criteria to be eligible for Eurostars funding: The project consortium must be led by an innovative SME from a Eurostars country. The project consortium must be composed of at least two entities that are independent from each other. Eureka Eurostars is the world's largest international funding programme for collaborative R&D projects led by innovative SMEs. descricao: Innowwide Innowwide is funded by the European Union as part of the European Partnership on Innovative SMEs Innowwide supports innovative small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs) and startups to assess the viability of research or commercial plans in international markets. The programme offers grants of 60,000 euro. The Innowwide programme provides grant funding to SMEs and startups so that they can run market feasibility projects in cooperation with local actors in the selected target country. Market feasibility projects allow SMEs to gain a deep understanding of the business environment in a specific target country. Some key outcomes from the project include: Understanding the technical feasibility of your product, process, or service in that market Understanding the viability of your business model Identifying key local legal, financial, political, cultural, and behavioural characteristics that could affect the deployment of your solution Identifying ideal ways to exploit your solution, including further research and innovation Funded projects receive a grant of 60,000 euro to assess the practical, technical, and economic feasibility of an innovative solution in a new market during a 6-month timeframe. Projects must come from an SME or startup in an EU Member State, Iceland, Israel, Norway, Switzerland, Türkiye, or the United Kingdom. They must be directed towards a target country in: Africa, the Americas, Asia, or Oceania. You can apply if you are an SME or startups from an EU Member State, Iceland, Israel, Norway, Switzerland, Türkiye or the United Kingdom. Applications to Innowwide must include an independent subcontractor that is established in the target country. Eureka Innowwide supports innovative SMEs and startups to assess the viability of research or commercial plans in international markets. Innowwide

descricao: Network Projects Flexible programme for international research and development cooperation The Network Projects programme provides access to funding for international research and development projects. It is designed to be flexible, with few limitations on the organisations that can participate in a project. This programme provides access to funding for research and development projects in a range of areas. As well as the general open call for projects, several sector, technology, or geographic specific calls are launched each year. Project applications can be made throughout the year and do not have to fit into any specific area of research, development or innovation. Projects are assessed by your National Funding Body. There are different types of call. A general call for projects is permanently open. National Funding Bodies also work together to launch specific calls for projects throughout the year. These calls are usually based on a particular theme or area of technology and are also often limited to certain countries. Depending on the details of the call and the country where you are applying from, support might be either as a grant or loan. A general call for projects is permanently open. Sector, technology, or geographic specific calls for projects in the Network Projects programme are also open several times a year. If a call is open, it will be listed below and on our open calls page. If no call is open, you can check back here later or subscribe to our newsletter to stay informed. Your project must meet several criteria to be eligible for funding under the Network Projects programme: Your project consortium must be made up of at least two entities that are independent from each other. Your project must be intended to research or develop a product, process, or service. Your project must be exclusively focused on civilian, non-military applications. The members of your project consortium must come from at least two participating countries. Eureka Network Projects provides access to funding for international R&D, flexibly, with few limitations on the organisations that can participate. Network Projects

descricao: Fast Track to the EIC Accelerator Continue innovating and scale-up your SME The Fast Track to the EIC Accelerator is part of the European Partnership on Innovative SMEs. The partnership is co-funded by the European Union through Horizon Europe . The Fast Track to the EIC Accelerator is designed to help startups and small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) that have completed, or are about to complete, a Eurostars-3-funded project to continue growing and developing. The scheme enables you to skip the first step (short proposal) and move directly to the second step (full proposal) of the EIC Accelerator. The EIC Accelerator supports startups, SMEs, and small mid-caps to scale up high impact innovations with the potential to create new markets or disrupt existing ones. The programme provides a unique combination of grant and investment funding, along with coaching, mentoring, and access to investors and corporates. Run by the European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA), the programme focuses on deep tech innovation and patient capital. In 2026, 634 million euro has been allocated to the EIC Accelerator. If you succeed in the Fast Track, your EIC Accelerator full proposal can be submitted to any of the following cut-offs in 2026: January 7, March 4, May 6, July 8, September 2, or November 4. Eureka Network has partnered with EISMEA to create this Fast Track as part of the European Partnership on Innovative SMEs . The Fast Track scheme allows startups, SMEs and small mid-caps that have completed a Eurostars project to skip the first step of the EIC Accelerator application. This year, the Eureka Network will allocate 20 full proposal tickets for the EIC Accelerator to selected participants. The Fast Track has several important advantages: By skipping the first step of the EIC Accelerator application, you will compete against fewer companies. Eureka’s expert evaluators will review your project and provide you with detailed feedback. You can pitch your project to an expert panel, helping to prepare for the formal EIC Accelerator pitch. You can receive a no-risk evaluation of your project idea. Eureka The Fast Track to the EIC Accelerator helps you continue innovating and scale-up your SME or startup. Fast Track to the EIC Accelerator

descricao: Globalstars Access new markets with global research and development Globalstars is a programme for organisations to connect with partners outside the Eureka network. The programme supports projects between companies in Eureka countries or regions and in leading and emerging markets around the world. Globalstars provides access to funding for research and development projects in a range of areas. As well as funding, Globalstars gives you a unique opportunity to work with organisations in countries and regions like Japan, Uruguay, India, and Taiwan. Globalstars provides funding to international research and development (R&D) projects. Projects must include at least one organisation from a Eureka country or region participating in the call, and the project consortium must also include at least one other independent organisation from the Globalstars country. Partners in the consortium can include other SMEs, large companies, universities, research institutions, and non-profits. Funding for Globalstars comes from National Funding Bodies in each country or region that is participating in a call. National Funding Bodies decide which organisations can receive funding, which activities can be funded, and how much funding is available. If a Globalstars call for projects is open, it will be listed below and on our open calls page. If no call is open, you can check back here later or subscribe to our newsletter to stay informed. Your project must meet several criteria to be eligible for funding under Globalstars. Your project consortium must be made up of at least two entities that are independent from each other. Your project must be intended to research or develop a product, process, or service. Your project must be exclusively focused on civilian, non-military applications. The members of your project consortium must come from at least two participating countries. At least one member must come from a Eureka country or region that is participating in the call, and one from a Globalstars country or region. No single organisation or country can be responsible for more than 70% of the project budget. Eureka Globalstars connects organisations with partners outside the Eureka network, helping you access new markets with global R&D. Globalstars

descricao: Investment Readiness The Investment Readiness programme is part of the European Partnership on Innovative SMEs. The partnership is co-funded by the European Union through Horizon Europe . The Investment Readiness programme connects you with multinational corporates and private investors. The programme can help your startup or SME grow in a range of sectors. Investment Readiness offers you the opportunity to get your solution in front of Eureka’s corporate partners. If successful, you will be invited to a meeting with the corporate to discuss future projects or investment with them. Eureka also organises missions to major international investment conferences, such as Web Summit and Singapore Week of Innovation and Technology (SWITCH). The Investment Readiness programme has two main activities: Eureka’s corporate partners set Corporate Challenges that you can respond to. If you are successful, you could collaborate with the corporate in a pilot project or access investment, depending on the challenge. We organise international missions to major investment conferences. Past missions have been to Web Summit and the Singapore Week of Innovation and Technology. These conferences give you the chance to meet international investors face-to-face. In 2026, we will organise three international missions for SMEs and startups to attend South Summit Brazil in Porto Alegre, Brazil from 25 to 27 March and the Swiss Biotech Days in Basel, Switzerland from 4 to 5 May. A third destination will be announced soon. Corporate Challenges are set throughout the year. You can find a list of all open Corporate Challenges on the calls page. If no challenges are open, you can check back later or subscribe to our newsletter to stay informed. Got an innovative idea? Explore our funding opportunities designed to support groundbreaking projects and help turn your vision into reality. Secure the resources you need to bring your ideas to life. Eureka The Investment Readiness programme connects you with multinational corporates and private investors, helping your startup or SME grow. Investment Readiness

descricao: Fast Track to the EIC Accelerator ‒ Call 4 Fast Track to the EIC Accelerator Continue innovating and scale-up your SME The Fast Track to the EIC Accelerator is part of the European Partnership on Innovative SMEs. The partnership is co-funded by the European Union through Horizon Europe . The Fast Track to the EIC Accelerator is designed to help startups and small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) that have completed, or are about to complete, a Eurostars-3-funded project to continue growing and developing. The scheme enables you to skip the first step (short proposal) and move directly to the second step (full proposal) of the EIC Accelerator. The EIC Accelerator supports startups, SMEs, and small mid-caps to scale up high impact innovations with the potential to create new markets or disrupt existing ones. The programme provides a unique combination of grant and investment funding, along with coaching, mentoring, and access to investors and corporates. Run by the European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA), the programme focuses on deep tech innovation and patient capital. In 2026, 634 million euro has been allocated to the EIC Accelerator. Eureka Network has partnered with EISMEA to create the Fast Track as part of the European Partnership on Innovative SMEs . The Fast Track has several important advantages: By skipping the first step of the EIC Accelerator application, you will compete against fewer companies. Eureka’s expert evaluators will review your project and provide you with detailed feedback. You may pitch your project to an EIC expert panel, facilitating your preparation for the formal EIC Accelerator pitch. You will receive a no-risk evaluation of your project idea, gaining an extra shot to the EIC Accelerator. descricao: Biotech call – September 2026 The Biotech Call for Network Projects is dedicated to foster biotech-related cooperation between the listed countries. Partners from countries that are not listed are welcome to join consortia if they organise their own national funding or self-finance their project work. The call complements Eureka’s Eurostars and Cluster calls published on Eureka Network’s website. Its unique characteristics are: small projects with clear implementation plan Each participating country evaluates and finances its own partners. To be successful, consortia applying for funding must be well-balanced, i.e. partners in each country provide relevant and innovative project contributions and added value for the international consortium. The Swiss Eureka Chair is organising the Global Innovation Summit on May 6, 2026, in Basel, back-to-back with the Swiss Biotech Day. Corporates, SMEs, startups, research institutions and universities from the entire Eureka Network and interested countries are invited to establish collaborations. The events will support participants in finding partners for the Biotech Call for Network Projects. Project applications with a clear innovation content and implementation plans in biotech areas like medicine, bioinformatics, pharmaceutical products and services, life sciences, digitalisation, or (bio)process technology (non-exhaustive list of cooperation areas) are welcome. The Dutch entrepreneurial spirit has historically been driven by a commitment to innovation and an open, international approach to trade. Particularly in the field of LSH, the Netherlands has gained a strong reputation. Global challenges around an ageing population, sufficient healthcare workers, overall affordability, and global disrupting health threats, ask for innovative solutions. This is where the Dutch LSH ecosystem has to jump in, not only for the Netherlands, but also to impact health around the world. At the same time, the Netherlands can learn a lot and benefit from innovative solutions and approaches in other countries. The Health~Holland International Strategy 2024 – 2027 focusses on exactly these opportunities, to maximize the impact of the Dutch LSH ecosystem on the global level and improve the Dutch ecosystem with lessons and knowledge from around the world. descricao: Eurostars Call 11 for projects – deadline September 2026 Eurostars is part of the European Partnership on Innovative SMEs. The partnership is co-funded by the European Union through Horizon Europe . Eurostars is a funding instrument that supports innovative SMEs and project partners (large companies, universities, research organisations and other types of organisations) by funding international collaborative R&D and innovation projects. By participating, organisations can access public funding for international collaborative R&D projects in all fields. To have a successful Eurostars application you must: Collaborate internationally, sharing expertise. Develop products, processes or services that can be easily commercialised. You can submit your R&D and innovation project application between 9 July 2026 and 10 September 2026 at 14:00 CET using our project platform ( myeurekaproject.org ). Your project consortium must have an innovative SME in the leading role, but it can also include other types of organisations like large companies, universities, research organisations and more. The amount of funding your organisation receives when you participate in a project is managed by your National Funding Body. Funding rules vary from country to country and your National Funding Body decides: which organisations can receive funding, which project activities can be funded If you are from a Eurostars country, you can discover what funding is available for your organisation in our ‘Country information’ section below, and by contacting your national or regional funding body using our contact form . Your National Funding Body may have maximum funding amount per project or project partner.
